title: PhilSa warns of Chinese rocket debris in PH waters
summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Space Agency (PhilSa) on Wednesday evening advised the public in the coastal communities to report any suspected debris found at sea after it confirmed the launch…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Space Agency (PhilSa) on Wednesday evening advised the public in the coastal communities to report any suspected debris found at sea after it confirmed the launch of China’s rocket.
China’s Long March 8A rocket was launched from the Hainan International Commercial Launch Center in Wenchang, Hainan, at around 9:33 p.m. (Philippine standard time) on Wednesday, according to PhilSa.
PhilSa said that rocket debris may have fallen within the following identified drop zones:

items: 97 nautical miles (NM) away from Patag Island
144 NM away from Bajo de Masinloc
190 NM away from El Nido, Palawan,
46 NM away from Puerto Princesa, Palawan
24 NM away from the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park
117 NM away from Hadji Muhtamad, Basilan (DZ 2)

blocks.text: “Details of the rocket drop zone were disclosed through a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) warning of an “aerospace flight activity.” PhilSA disseminated a pre-launch report to relevant government agencies and authorities prior to the launch,” it said in a statement.
PhilSa reminded the public to refrain from touching or retrieving the debris found at sea as it may contain toxic substances, such as rocket fuel.
“PhilSA reiterates its advice for the public to inform local authorities if suspected debris is sighted,” it said. /das
